rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape [16, 16384] yields size = 262,144. Host code condition `if (size >= 1024)` is true, so vectorized kernel is always used. The mutation is on line 48 in `hardsigmoid_kernel_scalar`, which is only launched when size < 1024. Since 262,144 >= 1024, the scalar kernel (and thus the mutation) is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes `blockIdx.x` to `blockIdx.y` in the scalar kernel's index calculation. However, the host-side dispatch logic branches on tensor size: tensors with >= 1024 elements use the vectorized kernel, while smaller tensors use the scalar kernel. The fixed input shape [16, 16384] has 262,144 elements, which always exceeds the 1024 threshold. Therefore, the vectorized kernel is always selected and the scalar kernel containing the mutation is never invoked. No value-level test can trigger execution of the mutated code path without changing the input shape.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation resides in dead code (scalar kernel) that is unreachable for inputs of size >= 1024. Killing this mutant would require testing with a tensor having fewer than 1024 elements, which violates the fixed-shape constraint.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing kernels with dispatch logic based on input characteristics, ensure the test suite covers all code paths (vectorized AND scalar kernels). Consider parameterizing tests with shapes that exercise both branches of the size-based dispatch, or flag mutations in unreachable code paths as equivalent under specific input contracts.
